title: Installer does not enforce the stdlib-only runtime dependency policy
reasoning: The fresh environment installs the wheel without --no-deps or validation that its metadata contains no Requires-Dist entries. A mispackaged release could consequently install third-party packages from an index, violating the project's stdlib-only runtime policy and expanding its network and supply-chain exposure.
reproduction: Build a clawpatch-supervise wheel with a Requires-Dist entry, provide it through CLAWPATCH_SUPERVISE_SOURCE with its SHA-256, and run the installer; pip resolves and installs the declared dependency.
recommendation: Use --no-deps and reject the installation before activation when the installed distribution metadata contains any Requires-Dist entries.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were linked for this feature, and no supplied test exercises a dependency-bearing wheel or asserts that package-index access is prohibited.
suggestedRegressionTest: Run the installer with a temporary wheel that declares a test dependency and assert that it fails without accessing a package index or activating either command.
minimumFixScope: Change the pip invocation in scripts/install.sh, add a zero-runtime-dependencies metadata validation, and add an installer regression test.

history.reasoning: The repair is present, but targeted validation could not run without writable temporary storage. ✅ Done — finding revalidated as uncertain.
